newsitem.title: UK: British small businesses fear single currency - survey.
newsitem.headline: British small businesses fear single currency - survey.

text.p: Small and medium-sized businesses in Britain fear participation in a single European currency would damage their business, undermine employment prospects and push up prices to consumers, according to a survey by business information group CCN.

Its poll of 2,500 senior managers in firms with annual turnover below 100 million pounds ($156.5 million) showed three out of four believe they would be able to invest less, while two-thirds expect interest rates and both corporate and personal taxes to rise under European monetary union (EMU).

"Our research shows that the majority of small and medium-sized enterprises expect there to be penalties from joining EMU, with no compensating increase in business," said Jo Howard of CCN's business information division.

"Less than half the companies in the survey believe they will actually sell more goods or services in Europe if Britain joins the single currency, while over three quarters believe it will stop them selling more outside Europe."
Support for EMU was strongest among companies in computing, the oil industry and health and household goods manufacturers.
Those least in favour included engineering, retail, construction, distribution, food manufacturing, media and leisure companies, the survey showed. ($1=.6388 Pound)
